== Character template ==

Hi there. Just thought I'd let you know that the reason I changed the character template was so that the [[Asmodean]] page worked properly. With both infoboxes calling for the WoT encyclopedia, it meant there was 2 links and also that the text was being moved around to make way for the second such link. I don't actually know why that page even has two infoboxes when others don't, but there we go. &mdash;[[User:Jaymach|Jaymach Ral'Tir]] <small>([[User talk:Jaymach|talk]])</small> 11:55, March 27, 2010 (UTC)
:There was some formatting that was missing from his page for the text problem. The two links are fine. The reason that he has the two infoboxes is mainly because of [[Aginor]] and [[Balthamel]]. When a character has been re-born or has assumed an alias for a long period of time, they get two (or more) infoboxes. I fixed the problem on Asmodean's page. Let me know if you have any more questions. :) ----[[User:Mainphramephreak|<span style="color:#000099;"> '''Willie'''</span>]] - [[User Talk:Mainphramephreak|<span style="color:#990099;">'''''HtS'''''</span>]] 12:10, March 27, 2010 (UTC)
::Yeah, I had actually removed the formatting because it was causing even bigger problems. With the "clear all" tag, the page looks like [http://img248.imageshack.us/img248/9536/asmodean.jpg this] on higher resolutions, whereas without it, the page looks like [http://img695.imageshack.us/img695/9536/asmodean.jpg this]. The other reason for adding the "if" statement to the template is because this wiki may eventually have pages that the WoT Encyclopedia doesn't have. For example, I'm likely to add pages on [[Lord]]s [[Argirin Darelos]] and [[Ballin Elamri]] who only exist in the [[CCG]], and so the WoT Encyclopedia don't have pages on them. Just seemed to make more sense to me. &mdash;[[User:Jaymach|Jaymach Ral'Tir]] <small>([[User talk:Jaymach|talk]])</small> 04:11, March 29, 2010 (UTC)

== Oath Rod ==

Hi. On the Oath Rod page it says that "Swearing oaths causes a tightening of the skin, which is responsible for the "ageless" look of Aes Sedai." I remember it being stated that the oaths feel tight on the skin but not that the feeling of constriction being the cause of the ageless look. I believe this to be speculation as i do not remember it being specifically stated in the series, however i may be wrong. Can you provide any verification?


Thanks.[[User:Rahl404|Rahl404]] 02:51, June 25, 2010 (UTC)

:Thanks for joining up! I changed the page to a somewhat better wording. We do know why it happens. The Oath Rod was originaly a binder for criminals. Break the law and you get a distinctive look that everyone knows. Kind of like a long-term branding. As for how, it is the "mechanics" of the rod. The "how" on several other devices, or even the One Power itself, isn't known. <!---This isn't ment to be sarcastic or demeaning. Just informative. --->How does the wording work now? ----[[User:Mainphramephreak|<span style="color:#000099;"> '''Willie'''</span>]] - [[User Talk:Mainphramephreak|<span style="color:#990099;">'''''HtS'''''</span>]] 03:03, June 25, 2010 (UTC)

::The conspiracy was in fact mentioned. I understand that you like the way words look to that of figures, but that does not explain why your preference trumps everyone else's. Shouldn't the preference of the creator an article trump that of later editors? For categories, It is not clear why you think so many articles need to be listed at the beginning of the category instead of under the alphabetical listing. Even assuming there is a good reason, your method is not the best way. It is preferable to use <nowiki>[[Category:Aes Sedai| ]]</nowiki>. ::::Actually, having looked, the only AS listed should have been in a lower category. There is simply no justification for any article other than [[Aes Sedai]] and [[Aes Sedai (Age of Legends)]] not being alphabetized in the normal way. -[[User:Rrius|Rrius]] 20:34, July 14, 2010 (UTC)

As it stood before I redid all of the character categorization, in any given category, if it contained both character pages and non-character pages, all of the non-character pages where categorized under the "space" heading and not under their respective letters. The trick you mentioned (<nowiki>[[Category:Aes Sedai| ]]</nowiki>), won't properly alphabetize those in the "space" heading. The order is detirmined by when they were added. However, now that there are no more characters in that category, it is fine that they are under their respective letter headings. 

As to the numbers issue, almost everywhere else on this wiki, the numbers have been spelled out where practical (i.e. not done with very large numbers). Also, as to the "creator" of an article, this is a wiki. No one "owns" any of the mainspace pages. It is common for numbers that can be expressed in one or two words to be spelled out, or expressed as numerals. Since almost all of the other pages spell them out, I decided to follow suit.

Please let me know if there is anything else I can help you with. ----[[User:Mainphramephreak|<span style="color:#000099;"> '''Willie'''</span>]] - [[User Talk:Mainphramephreak|<span style="color:#990099;">'''''HtS'''''</span>]] 22:13, July 14, 2010 (UTC)
:I noticed how the ordering works here and have acted accordingly. However, I suggest that where one article is the main one dealing with the category, it should be the only spaced one, and others put ahead of the humans should be <nowiki>[[Category:Aes Sedai|*]]</nowiki>, which will create a new asterisk section above the As.

:As to numbers, my point is not that a creator of an article owns it, but that no one does. Where something is merely a stylistic preference, I object to its being changed. Since you and I could wheel revert over the issue ''ad infinitum'', some means of choosing between the methods should exist. Since there is no neutral source to turn to, such as a WOT Wiki style guide, I think it makes the most sense that the first style choice made should prevail.

Also, as an aside, many wikis generally follow their subject's way of doing things. For example, since Star Trek is an American production, [http://memory-alpha.org Memory Alpha] uses American spelling. Since we are a wiki for a litterary work, it stands to reason to follow our subject's way of doing things. Take a look at {{Tgs|39}} where Egwene goes over a few things from Verin's book. Happy editing! ----[[User:Mainphramephreak|<span style="color:#000099;"> '''Willie'''</span>]] - [[User Talk:Mainphramephreak|<span style="color:#990099;">'''''HtS'''''</span>]] 22:20, July 14, 2010 (UTC)

If it is about the spelling of "grey", I try to use "gray", but despite being an American, I have always used "grey", just as I have always used "colour", "labour", and "behaviour". If it is neither of those things, I'd appreciate an explanation because I am genuinely in the dark. -[[User:Rrius|Rrius]] 22:57, July 14, 2010 (UTC)
::More to the point, if it is about numbers, the analogy isn't apt. == Graendal's status ==

The readers are lead (by the text) to think she is dead. Rand thinks she is dead. There is no supporting text for her survival; and finally after Rand balefired all of Natrin's Barrow, Ramshalan's compulsion disappears proving she was destroyed ([[TGS]], ch37). At least the status should be changed to "unknown". Having her status remain "ALIVE" is too misleading (unless you know something that we do not know and you are determined to keep this your own secret) the status must be changed to something other than "ALIVE". I suggest her status be changed to "Unknown". Respectfully, [[User:Ronmamita|Ronmamita]] 10:05, September 24, 2010 (UTC)

==For the New User Guide==
Hello again. I have an idea regarding a lack of structure here. We have AHA! as a guide to use for characters, but it doesn't really apply to many other categories - you can't really use it with plants, for example. It's not a major problem when you're editing a page, but when you create a page it can be almost overwhelming without a basic guide. So I think maybe create something like an AHA! for each vastly different category and have them on the user guide. For example, for plants it could be something like PUD! (properties, usage, distribution). If there were basic set structures, it might make each page a little cleaner, and hopefully encourage people to add more info because they will know where to put it. It might also reduce the amount of editing you personally need to do to get the pages up to scratch.

Simpler things that I think could be included in the guide:
*The use of American English
*Where ''[[New Spring]]'' and the [[Guide]] fit chronologically. Everything pre-Book 1 being historical is understandable. But when including appeared and mentioned info in the character templates, does our chronology or the character's chronology come first? [[Tsutama Rath|Tsutama]] is a good example because in the order of books published she first appeared in ''[[A Crown of Swords]]'' and next appeared in ''New Spring'', but in her chronology obviously she appears first in NS 
*Format regarding people's names. I think that full names should be used the first time they are mentioned in an article, and then should revert to first name only for subsequent mentions
*Proper usage of refs

Thanks, hope my suggestions are welcome :) [[User:Daea|Daea]] 17:46, February 8, 2011 (UTC)

Currently these characters are described in a main character page, with their "secondary" character redirecting back to the main character page. I was wondering why this is? http://wot.wikia.com/wiki/Elf_Fantasy_Fair_8_April_2001_-_report_by_Aan'allein

I have never licensed my reports under any license (so regular copyright applies), and am extremely unhappy with my reports now appearing to be licensed under the CC-BY-SA license. Therefor, I'm respectfully asking you to completely delete the above reports (not just editing them as I could do myself, but to completely remove them).

As much as possible, I would also like you to try and create a sense of awareness about licensing and copyright in this community, so that I don't have to file a similar claim _again_ a few years from now. Thanks. [[User:Aan`allein|Aan`allein]] 14:11, October 8, 2011 (UTC)
:According to Fair Use, as long as we give proper attribution, which we have on the articles, they can be used on this wiki. I would be more than happy to alter our {{tl|fairuse|Fair Use}} template add it to the pages. Please let me know if you have any other questions.---- {{User:Mainphramephreak/Sig/Subst}} 01:38, October 9, 2011 (UTC)
::I don't think this qualifies for fair use (the chief factor against it being that my original work is copied wholesale). The idea that crediting is necessary or sufficient to claim fair use is actually one of the common misunderstandings listed on the wikipedia article about fair use which is linked from the template. That said, if including that template is all which it takes to assert that the article is copyrighted and the CC-BY-SA license doesn't apply, then please proceed like that. In the book those words are set apart by italics, but of course on the page the whole quote is italicized so the italic effectiveness is lost.  I tried bolding the words to make up for the ineffectual functionality of italics in this context but that doesn't seem to be enough.  Is there something else we can do to the text, like give it a bigger font size, or make it red, or something like that, to make it really stand out? Finally, I thank you for putting up with me.  You arer a consummate diplomat, exhibiting the patience of Job.  I'm in this project for the long haul.  With AMOL coming out, um, soon, there'll be plenty of material to keep us busy improving the site.  Take care.

== Shadowspawn vs shadowspawn ==

Hi Willie:

Shadowspawn is a generalized category, like "people."  When I say "I want to talk to the English," then I capitalize English.  When I say "I want to talk to the People," I capitalize People, both are specific and Proper nouns. However, when I say "I want to talk to people," it should remain lower-case.  That was my reasoning with Shadowspawn.

Alas, however, you are correct.  Robert Jordan says to capitalize it, so in the future, capitalized it shall be.

Sigh.  1.)  The Master is always right. 2.)  When the Master is wrong, see rule 1.

(grin)

Take care.

[[User:Pedantic|Pedantic]] 20:37, April 21, 2012 (UTC)

P.S. I'll let you decide who I mean by "the Master."

== Brandon Sanderson Blog Posts ==

Crossposting to all the listed admins.

I'm Brandon Sanderson's assistant. There's a problem with having Brandon's blog posts on your wiki.
http://wot.wikia.com/wiki/Category:Brandon_Sanderson_Blog_entries

All your content is labeled as being licensed under CC-BY-SA, but Brandon's blog posts must be copyright Dragonsteel Entertainment, LLC. Under ideal circumstances we don't have a problem with you mirroring certain posts on your wiki, but they must not be relicensed. Because if they are licensed CC-BY-SA, people can make a printed book of Brandon's blog posts and sell it on Barnes & Noble:
http://www.barnesandnoble.com/w/a-wheel-of-time-brandon-sanderson-blog-entries-source-wikia/1035865816?ean=9781234699406

That is just not cool. The people making that book think it is legal because they got the text from your website, which says CC-BY-SA.

Please do something about this. We will contact Barnes & Noble separately, but the license needs to be cleared up on your site. If wikia terms don't allow material to be posted without being CC-BY-SA, please just link straight to Brandon's blog posts instead of mirroring.

I'm sorry that unscrupulous content scrapers made this necessary.

== Sword form ==

Regarding the undoing of my edit on [[Lightning of Three Prongs]]:

Unfortunately, it is my experience that many people who have little or no knowledge of martial arts, fencing or swordcraft misunderstand the term "sword form" and assume that it is referring to the shape of the sword, not the style with which it is wielded. This is particularly problematic in places where English is not a first language but is widely sponken; in Spanish, for example, ''forma de la espada'' specifically refers to the shape of the sword, with ''estilo de la espada'' or ''estilo de esgrima'' referring to the style. This is important, since WoT is read around the world and many might have some confusion regarding the term ''sword form''. Not making allowances for non-native English speakers (or even younger native speakers who don't have the breadth of knowledge to understand the difference) is a mistake. It is my opinion that every article on a sword form should specify that a sword form is a style or school of fencing to avoid even the possibility of confusion or misinterpretation.

--[[User:Sings-With-Spirits|Sings-With-Spirits]] ([[User talk:Sings-With-Spirits|talk]]) 01:19, November 30, 2012 (UTC)

:I completely understand that English is a difficult language, even for native speakers. I also understand that not everyone has in-depth knowledge of martial arts and swordcraft. However, making that distinction on each individual page, especially when the distinction is made on the main [[sword form]] article, seems too much to me. Also, most of the sword form pages contain wording indicative of movement or utilization, i.e. "movement of the form" and "aggressive strikes," that differentiates it from the shape of a sword. ---- {{User:Mainphramephreak/Sig/Subst}} 02:15, November 30, 2012 (UTC)

==Amico Nagoyin==
I wasn't certain who to message about this, but the page about Amico Nagoyin is wrong. They make a big deal about this paragraph in The Dragon Reborn, but the quote it incorrectly as: 

"No two were born in the same city, and no more than two in any one country. Amico Nagoyin was the youngest, only four years older than Egwene and I. Joiya Byir could be our grandmother.... ...What chance that thirteen women chosen solely because they were Darkfriends would be so neatly arrayed across age, across nations, across Ajahs? Shouldn’t there be perhaps three Reds, or four born in Cairhien, or just two the same age, if it was all chance?"

However, the actual quote from a version of the book I bought about a month ago states:



"No two were born in the same city, and no more than two in any one country. Amico Nagoyin was the youngest, <u>'''some fifteen yearls older than'''</u> Egwene and I. Joiya Byir could be our great-grandmother's great-grandmother....", then a couple paragraphs later: "...What chance that thirteen women chosen solely because they were Darkfriends would be so neatly arrayed across age, across nations, across Ajahs? Shouldn’t there be perhaps three Reds, or four born in Cairhien, or just two the same age, if it was all chance?"



Someone should definitely correct this.



Thanks
